findings.reason: The statement says every standard module has a unique simple head, but the definition permits reducible E and Step 3.2 proves this only when E is irreducible. For W={1}, E=1⊕1 gives Δ(E)=Δ(1)⊕Δ(1), whose head is not simple. Restrict this clause to irreducible labels; the finite-length and simple-quotient claims remain supported.

The internal residue and meridian-root formulas are consistent, but the GGOR parameter comparison needs an explicit generator identification: this definition chooses s_H by its eigenvalue on the conormal, while [GGOR §§3.1, 5.2.2–5.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0212036) states its Hecke root using a reflection s with a specified eigenvalue in its V-convention. Clarify whether the source generator is s_H or s_H^{-1}, and reindex k_{H,j} if needed; the present claim k_{H,j}=-r_{H,j}/e_H and root equality is not established without that translation.

Step 3.1 uses a reduced denominator in the localized polynomial UFD, but the cited supplier establishes that C[h] is a UFD, not that C[h][δ^{-1}] is. Add the elementary localization argument or write the denominator argument in C[h] and treat factors of δ as units.
